lessons.title: Listen and speak: polite words in the town
lessons.objective: Use polite words in daily situations: please, thank you, you are welcome, sorry, sir and madam.
lessons.course:
Polite words make people happy.
We say “Please” when we ask for something. We say “Thank you” when we receive something. The other person answers: “You are welcome.”
We say “Sorry” when we make a mistake. We call a man “sir” and a woman “madam”.

support.title: Say with the adult
support.text:
Please, madam.
Thank you, sir.
You are welcome.
Sorry!

lessons.model: At the market, Nfor buys two oranges. He says: “Two oranges, please, madam.” The seller gives them. Nfor says: “Thank you, madam.” She answers: “You are welcome.”
lessons.guided: Play the market: one person sells fruits, the other buys. Use please, thank you and you are welcome. Then the buyer drops a fruit by mistake and says sorry.
lessons.exercise: The shopkeeper gives you bread. What do you say?
lessons.remediation: Practise one polite word at a time with real gestures: give and receive a cup while saying thank you.
lessons.transfer: Use please and thank you at every meal today.
lessons.materials: A few fruits or pictures of fruits, a small basket.

practice.prompt: Match each situation with the polite word.
practice.answer: asking: Please; receiving: Thank you; mistake: Sorry.
practice.explanation: Each situation has its polite word.

practice.prompt: Someone says “Thank you” to you. What do you answer?
practice.explanation: “You are welcome” is the answer to “Thank you”.

practice.prompt: Listen and say after the voice.
practice.listen: Please, madam. Thank you, sir. You are welcome.
practice.answer: Please, madam. Thank you, sir. You are welcome.
practice.explanation: Speak clearly and kindly.

lessons.title: Read: short words with i, n, m, d
lessons.objective: Read the letter sounds i, n, m, d and short words of three sounds made with them.
lessons.course:
Four new sounds: i as in ink, n as in net, m as in mat, d as in dog.
With the sounds we know, we read short words: pin, tin, man, mat, dip, sit, map.
We point under each sound and read from left to right.

support.title: Read with the adult
support.text:
i  n  m  d
pin  man  map  dip  sit

lessons.model: The adult reads slowly: “m… a… p… map. There is a map of the town on the wall.”
lessons.guided: Change one letter to make a new word: man → mat → map. Read each new word aloud together.
lessons.exercise: Read the word: m – a – n.
lessons.remediation: Go back to two sounds (in, an), then add the first sound.
lessons.transfer: Look for the letters m and n on a sign or a box at home.
lessons.materials: Letter cards i, n, m, d, s, a, t, p.

practice.prompt: Put the letters in order to make “map”.
practice.explanation: Read the sounds from left to right.

practice.prompt: Which word starts with the sound d?
practice.explanation: d-i-p starts with d.

practice.prompt: Complete the word with the missing sound: m _ n (a grown-up boy).
practice.explanation: m-a-n: man.

lessons.title: Write: letters a to m
lessons.objective: Form the small letters a to m from left to right, on the line.
lessons.course:
Letters sit on the line. Some letters are short: a, c, e, i, m. Some letters are tall: b, d, f, h, k, l. The letter g goes below the line.
We start each letter at the right place and write from left to right.

support.title: Trace with the adult
support.text:
a b c d e f g
h i j k l m

lessons.model: The adult writes a slowly: “Round like a c, then a stick down.” Then d: “Round, then a tall stick.”
lessons.guided: Trace each letter on the model with a finger, then write it three times on the line. Say its sound each time.
lessons.exercise: Write the letters a, b, c on the line.
lessons.answer: a b c, written on the line from left to right.
lessons.remediation: Trace the letter in sand or with a finger on the table before using the pencil.
lessons.transfer: Write the first letter of the name of a shop or a place in your town.

practice.prompt: Write the letters d, e, f.
practice.answer: d e f, on the line.
practice.explanation: d is tall, e is short, f is tall.

practice.prompt: Put the letters in alphabet order.
practice.explanation: The alphabet has a fixed order.

practice.prompt: Which letter goes below the line?
practice.explanation: The tail of g goes below the line.

lessons.title: One and many: plurals with s
lessons.objective: Make the plural of countable nouns by adding s, and use them in short sentences.
lessons.course:
One thing is singular: one house, one car. More than one is plural. To make the plural, we often add s: two houses, three cars.
In the town we see: a shop, two shops; a road, many roads.

support.title: Say with the adult
support.text:
one shop → two shops
one car → three cars

lessons.model: The adult counts pictures: “One bus. Two buses… no, here is an easy one: one car, two cars, three cars.”
lessons.guided: Use objects or drawings: show one, then two. Say the noun, then the plural with s. Listen to the s at the end.
lessons.remediation: Work only with nouns that add s without a change of sound (car, cup, book) before others.
lessons.transfer: Count things on the road: “three cars, two bikes”.
lessons.materials: Small objects or pictures in groups of one and more.

practice.prompt: Add s to make the plural.
practice.text: one shop, two shop[[s]]; one road, four road[[s]]
practice.explanation: Add s for more than one.

practice.prompt: Which one is plural?
practice.explanation: Markets ends with s: more than one.

practice.prompt: Write the plural of “car”.
practice.explanation: car + s = cars.

lessons.title: Sorting by colour, shape and size
lessons.objective: Differentiate objects by their attributes (colour, shape, size) and sort them.
lessons.course:
We can sort the same objects in different ways: by colour (red, blue), by shape (round, square), by size (big, small).
We say the rule: “I sorted by colour.”
lessons.model: At the market, the adult sorts fruits: “Big oranges here, small oranges there. I sorted by size.”
lessons.guided: Sort buttons or bottle tops by colour, then mix them and sort them by size. Say the rule each time.
lessons.exercise: Ayuk puts the big balls in one basket and the small balls in another. How did he sort?
lessons.remediation: Sort by colour only, with two colours.
lessons.transfer: Sort the shoes at home: big ones and small ones.
lessons.materials: Bottle tops or buttons of different colours and sizes.

practice.prompt: How are these sorted? red cup, red ball, red hat.
practice.explanation: They are all red.

practice.prompt: Match each object with its group.
practice.answer: lorry: big; ant: small; tree: big.
practice.explanation: We sorted by size.

practice.prompt: Say one way to sort fruits at the market.
practice.answer: By colour, by size or by kind.
practice.explanation: There are many ways to sort.

lessons.title: Numbers 11 to 20 in figures and in words
lessons.objective: Count, read and write numbers from 11 to 20 in figures and in words.
lessons.course:
After ten come: eleven (11), twelve (12), thirteen (13), fourteen (14), fifteen (15), sixteen (16), seventeen (17), eighteen (18), nineteen (19), twenty (20).
14 is one ten and four units.
lessons.model: The adult shows a bundle of ten sticks and four loose sticks: “Ten and four make fourteen: 14.”
lessons.guided: Make numbers with a bundle of ten and loose sticks. Read the number, then write it in figures.
lessons.remediation: Count objects from 10 to 15 first, one by one.
lessons.transfer: Count the houses in your street up to 20.

practice.prompt: One ten and three units. Which number?
Match the number with its word.
practice.explanation: Read the figure, then the word.

practice.prompt: Put the numbers in order.
practice.explanation: Each number is one more.

lessons.title: Adding within 20
lessons.objective: Add two small numbers within 20 using objects and the signs + and =.
lessons.course:
To add is to put together. 3 mangoes and 2 mangoes make 5 mangoes.
We write: 3 + 2 = 5. The sign + means “and”, the sign = means “makes”.
lessons.model: The adult puts 6 oranges in a basket, then 3 more: “6 and 3 more: 7, 8, 9. 6 + 3 = 9.”
lessons.guided: Make the two groups with stones, put them together and count. Write the addition.
lessons.exercise: A seller has 8 tomatoes. She gets 4 more. How many tomatoes now?
lessons.remediation: Count on from the bigger number with your fingers: 8… 9, 10, 11, 12.
lessons.transfer: At home, add the people sitting at the table with those who come later.

practice.explanation: Count on from 5: 6, 7, 8, 9.

practice.prompt: Complete the additions.
practice.explanation: Count on from the first number.

practice.prompt: What does the sign + mean?
practice.explanation: + means we add.

lessons.title: The number line up to 20
lessons.objective: Locate numbers on a number line up to 20 and move forward on it.
lessons.course:
A number line shows numbers in order, with the same space between them: 0, 1, 2, … 20.
To add, we jump forward. From 5, two jumps forward land on 7.
lessons.model: The adult draws a line on the ground with chalk, numbers 0 to 20. A child stands on 4 and jumps 3 times: “5, 6, 7. I am on 7.”
lessons.guided: Walk on a number line drawn on the ground. Find a number, then jump forward to add.
lessons.exercise: On the number line, start at 10 and jump 5 times forward. Where are you?
lessons.remediation: Use a line from 0 to 10 first.
lessons.transfer: Draw a number line in the yard and play with a brother or a sister.
lessons.materials: Chalk, an open space, a stone to mark the place.

practice.prompt: Which number comes just after 12 on the number line?
practice.explanation: One step forward from 12 is 13.

practice.prompt: Start at 6 and jump 4 times forward. Where do you land?
Put these numbers in their place on the line, from left to right.
practice.explanation: Smaller numbers are on the left.

lessons.title: Animals of the village and their homes
lessons.objective: Identify domestic animals of the village, say where each one lives and how we care for it.
lessons.course:
Domestic animals live with people: the goat, the sheep, the pig, the dog, the cat, the hen.
Each one has a home: the hen sleeps in a coop, the goat in a pen, the pig in a sty, the dog in a kennel.
We give them food and clean water, and we keep their homes clean. We do not go near an animal we do not know.
lessons.model: In Nfor’s compound, the hens sleep in the coop at night. In the morning he gives them maize and clean water.
lessons.guided: Look at pictures of animals and their homes. Put each animal next to its home and say: “The hen lives in a coop.”
lessons.remediation: Start with two animals the child sees every day.
lessons.transfer: Find out which animals live in your compound or your street and where they sleep.
lessons.materials: Pictures of domestic animals and of their homes.

practice.prompt: Match each animal with its home.
practice.answer: hen: coop; pig: sty; dog: kennel.
practice.explanation: Each domestic animal has its own home.

practice.prompt: Which one is a domestic animal?
practice.explanation: A goat lives with people; lions and elephants are wild.

practice.prompt: Say one way to care for a domestic animal.
practice.answer: Give it food and clean water, keep its home clean.
practice.explanation: Animals need food, water and a clean home.

lessons.title: Je m’appelle…
lessons.objective: Se présenter en français : dire son nom et son âge.
lessons.course:
Pour me présenter, je dis : « Je m’appelle Bih. » (My name is Bih.) « J’ai six ans. » (I am six years old.)
Pour présenter un ami : « Voici Neba. » (This is Neba.)

support.title: Dis avec l’adulte
support.text:
Je m’appelle …
J’ai six ans.
Voici mon ami.

lessons.model: Manka se lève et dit : « Bonjour ! Je m’appelle Manka. J’ai six ans. » Puis elle montre son ami : « Voici Tabi. »
lessons.guided: Fais un cercle avec la famille. Chacun dit : « Je m’appelle … » puis présente son voisin : « Voici … ».
lessons.remediation: Dis seulement « Je m’appelle … » plusieurs fois, puis ajoute l’âge.
lessons.transfer: Présente un membre de ta famille en français : « Voici ma maman. »
lessons.materials: Une balle à se passer pour donner la parole.

practice.prompt: Remets les mots dans l’ordre.
practice.explanation: On commence par « Je ».

practice.prompt: Complète.
practice.explanation: Pour l’âge, on dit « ans ».

practice.prompt: Écoute et répète.
practice.listen: Je m’appelle Neba. J’ai six ans.
practice.answer: Je m’appelle Neba. J’ai six ans.
practice.explanation: Parle lentement et clairement.

lessons.title: People who lead our village or town
lessons.objective: Identify some authorities of the community and show them respect.
lessons.course:
Some people lead and serve the community: the chief, the quarter head, the mayor, the head teacher, the religious leaders.
We respect them: we greet them politely and we listen when they speak.
lessons.model: The quarter head visits Nfor’s compound. Nfor greets him: “Good morning, sir,” and brings him a chair.
lessons.guided: Name the leaders you know in your village or town. Play a visit: greet a leader politely.
lessons.remediation: Start with leaders the child knows: the head teacher, the chief.
lessons.transfer: Find out the name of the chief or quarter head of your area.
lessons.materials: Pictures of community places (palace, town hall, school).

practice.prompt: Match each leader with the place.
practice.answer: chief: palace; mayor: town hall; head teacher: school.
practice.explanation: Each leader serves in a place.

practice.prompt: How do we show respect to a leader?
practice.explanation: We greet leaders and listen to them.

practice.prompt: Say the name of one leader of your school.
practice.explanation: The head teacher leads the school.

lessons.title: Folding a paper fan
lessons.objective: Fold paper to produce a simple object: a fan.
lessons.course:
Folding means bending paper along a line. To make a fan, we fold the paper forward, then backward, again and again, like steps. Then we pinch one end.
We fold slowly and press each fold well.
lessons.model: The adult folds a sheet: “Forward, backward, forward, backward.” Then pinches the bottom: “Here is a fan for the hot afternoon.”
lessons.guided: Take a sheet of paper. Fold it forward and backward together with the adult. Decorate the fan.
lessons.exercise: How do we fold a fan?
lessons.answer: Forward, backward, forward, backward, then we pinch one end.
lessons.remediation: Fold big strips first, then smaller ones.
lessons.transfer: Make a fan for someone at home.
lessons.materials: Sheets of paper or old newspaper, coloured pencils, a rubber band.

practice.prompt: Put the steps in order.
practice.explanation: Follow the steps one by one.

practice.prompt: What do we use a fan for?
practice.explanation: A fan moves air when it is hot.

practice.prompt: Draw the fan you made.
practice.explanation: Draw the folds.

lessons.title: Colours of the market
lessons.objective: Colour objects with appropriate colours and name the colours.
lessons.course:
Things have colours: a ripe banana is yellow, a pear (avocado) is green, a tomato is red, an orange is orange, plantain leaves are green.
We choose the right colour to colour a drawing.
lessons.model: The adult shows a basket of fruits: “The tomato is red. The banana is yellow. The avocado is green.”
lessons.guided: Colour a drawing of a market stall with the right colours. Say each colour aloud.
lessons.exercise: What colour is a ripe tomato?
lessons.remediation: Match real fruits with crayons of the same colour.
lessons.transfer: At the market, name the colours of five things you see.
lessons.materials: Drawing of fruits, coloured pencils, real fruits.

practice.prompt: Match each fruit with its colour.
practice.answer: banana: yellow; avocado: green; tomato: red.
practice.explanation: Each fruit has its colour.

practice.prompt: Colour a fruit with the right colour.
practice.answer: A fruit coloured with its real colour.
practice.explanation: Look at a real fruit to choose the colour.

practice.prompt: Which colour is a ripe mango?
practice.explanation: Ripe mangoes are yellow or orange.

lessons.title: Skipping and galloping
lessons.course:
To skip, we step and hop on one foot, then step and hop on the other foot. To gallop, one foot stays in front and the other foot chases it, like a horse.
We move in a free space and look where we go.
lessons.model: The adult skips across the yard: step-hop, step-hop. Then gallops like a horse.
lessons.guided: Skip from one line to another, then gallop back. Try to the rhythm of claps.
lessons.exercise: Which animal do we copy when we gallop?
lessons.remediation: Practise the hop on one foot first.
lessons.transfer: Skip to the beat of a song at home.

practice.prompt: Which movement is “step-hop, step-hop”?
practice.explanation: Skipping is step and hop.

practice.prompt: Put in order: how to skip.
practice.explanation: Skipping repeats step and hop.

practice.prompt: Where do we move when we skip and gallop?
practice.answer: In a free space, looking where we go.
practice.explanation: We avoid bumping into others.

lessons.title: Greetings in our language
lessons.objective: Greet people in the home language at different periods of the day and answer politely.
lessons.course:
In every language, we greet people in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening and at night, and we answer politely.
In many cultures, children greet elders first and with respect: a bow, both hands, or kneeling, depending on the family.
lessons.model: The family says the morning greeting in its language. The child repeats it and greets his grandmother with respect.
lessons.guided: Ask the adult the greetings of the morning and the night in the family language. Practise them with gestures of respect.
lessons.exercise: Say the morning greeting in your family language.
lessons.answer: The morning greeting said in the family language.
lessons.transfer: Greet an elder in the family language tomorrow morning.

practice.prompt: Say the night greeting in your family language.
practice.answer: The night greeting in the family language.
practice.explanation: Ask an adult to help you.

practice.prompt: Whom do children greet first in many cultures?
practice.explanation: Greeting the elders first shows respect.

practice.prompt: Match each greeting with its time.
practice.explanation: Greetings change with the time of day.

lessons.title: Messages in the village: the drum, the town crier and the phone
lessons.objective: Identify traditional and modern tools for communication and say how they help people.
lessons.course:
Long ago in villages, people sent messages with the talking drum, the town crier who walked and announced the news, or a messenger. Today we also use the phone, the radio and the television.
All of them help people share news.
lessons.model: In Nfor’s village, the town crier announces a meeting with a bell. Nfor’s uncle in the town learns the news by phone.
lessons.guided: Sort pictures: traditional tools (drum, town crier, messenger) and modern tools (phone, radio, TV).
lessons.exercise: Name one traditional tool for sending messages.
lessons.answer: For example: the talking drum or the town crier.
lessons.remediation: Compare two tools only: the drum and the phone.
lessons.transfer: Ask an elder how news was sent when he was a child.

practice.prompt: Match each tool with its group.
practice.answer: drum: traditional; town crier: traditional; phone: modern.
practice.explanation: Some tools are old, some are new.

practice.prompt: Which is the fastest way to send news to a far town today?
practice.explanation: A phone call reaches far quickly.

practice.prompt: What do all these tools help people to do?
practice.explanation: They are tools for communication.
